The main takeaway from our work is that
time-resolved crystallographic data can be used to identify and characterize intermediates, and to test chemical kinetic models.

time-resolved crystallographic data can provide the basis for a consistent set of reaction intermediates and reaction mechanisms, and thus provide a powerful approach to study protein reaction mechanisms.

time-resolved crystallography is capable of providing the structures of reaction intermediates, which can then be combined with chemical kinetic analysis to yield a consistent set of reaction intermediates and chemical kinetic mechanism.
